newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta share end lower but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta share end lower but off lows.

text.p: Jakarta share price index ended lower but off its daily low on Wednesday due to falls in few big-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.25 points, or 0.40 percent, to close at 559.70 points. Losers led gainers 46 to 24, with 39 counters unchanged.
Brokers said market was likely to be mixed on Thursday as some foreigners waited for further indications of the U.S interest movements.
"But some others consider that the prevailing prices of some blue chips counters are cheap. There is still a potential for those stocks to soar but volume remains limited," a foreign broker said.
A local broker said he was waiting for more positive issues to improve broad market sentiment and boost buying.
Car assembler Astra International topped the active list with 6.6 million shares, up 25 rupiah to 2,950 rupiah on market talk of a possible rights issue.
Brokers said it was also due to a report saying the firm would launch a new version of the Kijang, company's popular car.
Lippo Securities, Lippo Life and Lippo Life were also among the active list on speculation that Lippo Group's restructuring plan for its three financial unit would be successful.
Brokers said some foreign operators buying actively on those stocks after on positive perceptions following an analyst meeting with Lippo chairman James Riady.
They also said there was a speculation the restructuring plan, including internal acquisitions among those three financial units, would win the shareholders approval on September 27.

Lippo Securities rose 50 rupiah to 1,400 rupiah on a volume of 4.5 million shares. Lippo Bank rose 25 rupiah to 3,400 rupiah on a volume of 1.2 million shares while Lippo Life traded unchanged at 1,875 rupiah on a volume of 1.1 million shares.
Heavyweight cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 100 rupiah to 22,200 on a volume of 1.1 million shares after fell to 21,200 rupiah in early trade.
Brokers said the early fall was due to its first half result not being in line with expectations.

But brokers said Sampoerna rose in late trade due to a perception that its current prices was quite cheap and an expectation the second half results would be stronger after talk that the firm intented to increase its cigarette prices.
